statement: NVIDIA's AI infrastructure platform can sustain attractive growth and economics if demand remains durable, architecture transitions execute on time, its software and system advantages withstand substitution, and market access remains commercially meaningful, especially in China. These assumptions require separate evidence; a product or earnings headline alone does not justify rewriting the thesis.
notices: This NVIDIA baseline is not a stock valuation or a buy/sell recommendation.
boundaries: Source coverage is a design map. Automated acquisition and Check for Updates have not started; no monitored-through checkpoint exists.

Market access is a separate fifth driver, with China the focus requested by the owner. NVIDIA's own exposure and licensing disclosures are observable; official policy/export-control feeds remain outside this slice.

NVIDIA-only sources cannot independently verify customer returns, compute-market slack, Token prices/API volumes, CoWoS/HBM capacity allocations, customer accelerator advantages or third-party benchmarks. These watches are explicit monitoring gaps.

The owner's mid-weak customer-built accelerator signal and weak benchmark signal retain their stated strengths. Neither is an automatic thesis change; workload comparability, persistence, magnitude and review windows need human judgment.
Token/API measures are demand proxies. Lower prices alone require interpretation of comparable units, workloads and efficiency; they do not establish a market-wide supply/demand balance.

drivers.title: AI infrastructure demand durability
drivers.statement: Durable AI infrastructure demand can support NVIDIA Data Center growth.
drivers.core_assumption: Customer deployment demand persists beyond a single purchasing cycle; NVIDIA's disclosures are an incomplete proxy for customer economics. Aggregate demand for AI training and inference compute continues to exceed total market supply.
drivers.importance: Product strength only produces durable growth if customers keep deploying compute.
drivers.what_to_watch: Reported Data Center growth, forward guidance and management's demand/deployment commentary; compute idleness, subleasing and rental prices; Token prices and API call volumes. Independent customer utilization, returns and market-wide supply/demand remain gaps.

falsifiers.condition: Over the next two quarterly disclosures, Data Center growth slows in both periods and forward guidance or management commentary indicates sustained weaker deployment demand.
Compute capacity appears idle, is offered for sublease, or is repriced lower in the market.

watch_items.title: NVIDIA demand disclosures
watch_items.question: Do consecutive NVIDIA disclosures show slowing Data Center growth and weaker forward deployment demand?
watch_items.observation_scope: NVIDIA-reported Data Center revenue and growth, guidance and management demand/deployment commentary.
watch_items.cannot_verify: NVIDIA revenue growth does not independently prove customers' end demand, utilization or ROI. Absence of weak-demand language is not confirmation of this driver.

watch_items.title: Independent customer economics
watch_items.question: Do customers' independent utilization and returns corroborate durable deployment demand?
watch_items.observation_scope: Independent customer utilization, spending commitments and returns on AI infrastructure.
watch_items.gap_reason: NVIDIA-only documents cannot independently observe customer utilization or returns. External customer sources are not connected.

watch_items.title: Compute market slack and pricing
watch_items.question: Is compute capacity idle, offered for sublease or repriced lower in the market?
watch_items.observation_scope: Comparable compute utilization, capacity subleasing and rental prices across the market; geographic scope, units and observation window require owner confirmation.
watch_items.gap_reason: NVIDIA-only disclosures cannot independently observe market-wide idle capacity, subleasing or compute rental prices. External compute-market sources are not connected.

watch_items.title: Token prices and API call volumes
watch_items.question: Do Token prices and API call volumes support durable AI training and inference demand?
watch_items.observation_scope: Token prices and API call volumes across comparable services and workloads; these are demand proxies and do not measure total training/inference compute or market supply.
watch_items.gap_reason: Independent Token pricing and API usage sources are not connected. NVIDIA-only materials cannot independently establish these market-wide measures.

drivers.title: Product and supply ramp execution
drivers.statement: Architecture transitions can reach production and customer deployment without a material product gap.
drivers.core_assumption: New-platform supply and deployment can ramp while the prior generation continues serving customers. CoWoS and HBM are the key constraints, and NVIDIA holds priority allocations in critical production capacity.
drivers.importance: Demand cannot become revenue if production, quality or delivery fails.
drivers.what_to_watch: Changes to NVIDIA's announced production/deployment timetable, supply constraints and transition commentary in MD&A, risk factors and earnings materials. TSMC CoWoS monthly capacity and expansion plans, NVIDIA's share of CoWoS allocations, and HBM supply/allocation constraints. Independent supplier capacity and allocation data remain gaps.

falsifiers.condition: In the next two quarterly updates, NVIDIA discloses a production or deployment delay of at least one quarter versus its prior announced schedule, or supply disruption that materially impairs the revenue outlook.

watch_items.title: Production and deployment timetable
watch_items.question: Has NVIDIA revised its announced production/deployment schedule or disclosed a material supply disruption?
watch_items.observation_scope: NVIDIA's announced schedules and disclosed supply/transition risks; undisclosed supplier yields are not independently verified.
watch_items.cannot_verify: Unreported manufacturing yields and customer-site deployment progress cannot be independently checked. NVIDIA-only coverage is limited to disclosed milestones.

watch_items.title: CoWoS capacity and NVIDIA allocation
watch_items.question: Do TSMC's CoWoS monthly capacity and expansion plans, NVIDIA's allocation share and HBM constraints support the ramp assumption?
watch_items.observation_scope: TSMC CoWoS monthly capacity and expansion plans; NVIDIA's share of CoWoS allocations; HBM capacity and priority allocations, with consistent units and periods.
watch_items.gap_reason: NVIDIA may discuss its own supply constraints, but NVIDIA-only materials cannot independently establish TSMC capacity or NVIDIA's allocation share. Supplier and allocation sources are not connected.

drivers.title: Software and system competitive advantage
drivers.statement: Software adoption, system integration and switching costs can preserve NVIDIA's platform advantage.
drivers.core_assumption: Alternative accelerators or customer-built systems do not materially displace NVIDIA across major workloads; ecosystem expansion supports adoption rather than masking weak economics.
drivers.importance: Alternative platforms could weaken both demand and the economic value captured by NVIDIA.
drivers.what_to_watch: NVIDIA's competition, platform adoption and pricing disclosures; independent workload migration, competitor performance and ecosystem returns remain gaps. Customer-built accelerators' performance and cost on comparable workloads, and third-party benchmark results; retain the owner's mid-weak and weak signal labels.

falsifiers.condition: Within the next four quarterly disclosures, NVIDIA reports material customer workload migration, lost platform adoption or competitive pricing pressure that weakens its software/system advantage.
Customer-built accelerators establish a structural performance or cost advantage (mid-weak signal).
NVIDIA no longer leads in third-party evaluation benchmarks (weak signal).

watch_items.title: NVIDIA competitive disclosures
watch_items.question: Does NVIDIA disclose material adoption loss, workload migration or competitive pricing pressure?
watch_items.observation_scope: NVIDIA's own competitive risk, adoption and pricing commentary. Company claims alone do not establish the moat.
watch_items.cannot_verify: Company platform claims cannot independently verify market share, real workload TCO or switching costs. No disclosed migration does not prove that customers stayed.

watch_items.title: Independent substitution evidence
watch_items.question: Do independently observed workload migrations or competitor results undermine NVIDIA's platform advantage?
watch_items.observation_scope: Independent customer migration, competitor performance and ecosystem returns.
watch_items.gap_reason: NVIDIA-only materials do not provide independent competitor or customer adoption evidence. Competitor and customer sources are not connected.

watch_items.title: Customer-built accelerator advantage
watch_items.question: Do customer-built accelerators have a structural performance or cost advantage (mid-weak signal)?
watch_items.observation_scope: Independent customer accelerator comparisons on like-for-like workloads, performance and total cost; the structural advantage and review window require owner confirmation.
watch_items.gap_reason: Independent customer-built accelerator performance and cost sources are not connected. NVIDIA's own claims cannot establish or rule out a structural customer advantage.

watch_items.title: Third-party benchmark leadership
watch_items.question: Does NVIDIA cease to lead in third-party evaluation benchmarks (weak signal)?
watch_items.observation_scope: Independent benchmark leadership by comparable workload, hardware/software version and evaluation method; a weak signal does not automatically invalidate the driver.
watch_items.gap_reason: Third-party evaluation sources are not connected. NVIDIA-only materials do not independently establish benchmark leadership.

drivers.title: Profitability and gross margin durability
drivers.statement: Platform value and product economics can sustain attractive profitability through transitions.
drivers.core_assumption: Pricing and product mix can offset input costs and temporary transition pressure without persistent erosion of gross margin.
drivers.importance: Revenue growth must retain economic value rather than be consumed by recurring cost or pricing pressure.
drivers.what_to_watch: Comparable GAAP revenue, cost of revenue or gross profit in XBRL, gross margin guidance and explanations of transition effects in earnings materials.

falsifiers.condition: Across the next two reported quarters, GAAP gross margin declines in both periods and NVIDIA guides to continued pressure without a stated recovery path, beyond its disclosed temporary transition effects.

watch_items.title: Gross margin and transition economics
watch_items.question: Do comparable GAAP margins and guidance indicate persistent compression beyond temporary transition effects?
watch_items.observation_scope: NVIDIA GAAP XBRL facts where available, validated earnings quotations and gross margin guidance; no consensus feed.
watch_items.cannot_verify: Reported margins do not independently establish pricing power or isolate structural causes. GAAP/non-GAAP and one-off items require comparable treatment; no automated XBRL check is running here.

drivers.title: Market access, especially China
drivers.statement: Access to the China AI infrastructure market can remain a meaningful contributor to NVIDIA's growth within regulatory and licensing constraints.
drivers.core_assumption: Permitted products and licenses allow commercially meaningful sales in China; market-access restrictions do not persistently remove this growth opportunity.
drivers.importance: Strong demand is insufficient when export rules, licensing or regional restrictions prevent delivery or strand inventory.
drivers.what_to_watch: NVIDIA's disclosed China exposure, sales, licensing status and permitted-product changes; independent export-control rules, licensing decisions and implementation remain gaps.

falsifiers.condition: Across the next two quarterly disclosures, NVIDIA reports regulatory or licensing constraints that prevent commercially meaningful China sales, with no disclosed recovery path.

watch_items.title: NVIDIA China market-access disclosures
watch_items.question: Does NVIDIA disclose persistent licensing or regulatory constraints that prevent commercially meaningful China sales?
watch_items.observation_scope: NVIDIA's own reported China exposure, sales and revenue effects, licensing status and permitted-product changes; independent policy verification is outside this watch.
watch_items.cannot_verify: NVIDIA-only disclosures cannot independently establish legal interpretation, the scope of individual licenses, future approvals or customer delivery. No disclosed restriction is not proof of unrestricted access.

watch_items.title: Independent China market-access rules
watch_items.question: Do independent export-control rules and licensing decisions corroborate the disclosed China-access risks?
watch_items.observation_scope: Official export-control rules, licensing decisions and implementation affecting China market access, independently of NVIDIA's characterization.
watch_items.gap_reason: Official policy and licensing sources are outside this NVIDIA-only slice and are not connected. Company disclosures do not independently verify the operative rules.

parts.text: On 2026-08-26 NVIDIA published its Q2 FY2027 results release (Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1). Its outlook for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 includes the sentence quoted below, which is the only mention of China in that release.
parts.quote: NVIDIA is not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China in its outlook.

parts.text: This is management's planning assumption for the third quarter of fiscal 2027, not a reported result. The release gives no reason, does not mention export controls or licensing, and does not discuss a recovery path.

It bears on D5's core assumption that permitted products and licenses allow commercially meaningful sales in China, and may weaken it. It is a single forward-looking data point from one source; this system has not assessed it, and its weight is a human judgment.

D5.F1 is not recorded as triggered. It requires NVIDIA to report, across two quarterly disclosures, regulatory or licensing constraints that prevent commercially meaningful China sales, with no disclosed recovery path; this outlook sentence does not itself say that. Equally, nothing here confirms D5: later disclosures have not been checked, and independent export-control evidence (W5.2) remains a monitoring gap. Only your explicit decision changes a Standing Thesis.
